title: Work and Laziness
lead: Work in the Bible, from the garden given to Adam to keep, through the Sabbath that limits it and the wisdom sayings that praise diligence and mock the lazy, to Paul's call to work with one's hands.

sections.b: Before the fall the man is put in the garden "to work it and to guard it" (Genesis 2:15); after it, toil becomes painful (Genesis 3:17–19). The Sabbath sets a limit on work for everyone in the household, slaves and animals included (Exodus 20:8–11; Deuteronomy 5:12–15). Proverbs praises the diligent and laughs at the lazy man who will not get out of bed, finish his meal or plow in season (Proverbs 6:6–11; Proverbs 10:4–5; Proverbs 12:24; Proverbs 26:13–16), while also warning that toil adds nothing to the LORD's blessing (Proverbs 10:22; Psalm 127:1–2). Ecclesiastes asks what lasting gain there is in all of it (Ecclesiastes 2:18–24). Paul works with his own hands and tells the Thessalonians that anyone unwilling to work should not eat (2 Thessalonians 3:6–12; compare Ephesians 4:28).
